thread:
alex: Pager: surge in external actionproxy requests causing fn-call backlog and malformed structured outputs. seeing 5xx from agent-proxy and increased latency. Customers on free and standard plans are experiencing truncated tool responses. paging oncall.
maria: on it. do we have tenant list? any obvious hot tenants?
alex: early signs point to a handful of high-throughput tenants + a spike in a public community app. sample logs:
```
2026-03-17T12:03:02Z agent-proxy: 502 write kv cache timeout tenant=t-4823 fn=invoke-tool status=502 latency=1.2s
2026-03-17T12:03:03Z router: queue depth=1800 model=redwood-2-7b structured_output=true
```

tim: re-routing text-only fallback for tier=free and tier=dev might help. can we soft-quarantine tool calls for those plans first?
ryan: propose soft-quarantine + backpressure: reduce max_concurrent_calls per-tenant, set structured_output=false for fallback, and add a top-level rate limit for agent-proxy. non-blocking changes via runtime flags.
jess: notify support: some customers will see degraded features. i'll prepare a short blurb for status page once we have the mitigation decided.
maria: here's a safe knob I can flip via admin API to enact soft-quarantine for plan=free,dev:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/runtime/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"plan:free,dev","overrides":{"enable_tool_calls":false,"structured_output_mode":"text_only","max_concurrent_calls":2}}'
```
maria: i'll apply on dev plans first, monitor 60s, then expand if flux drops.
alex: +1. what about standard paid tenants? we should avoid cutting them unless necessary. maybe enforce rate-limits per-tenant and bump throttling for 3rd-party agents.
tim: i can push a runtime policy rule to limit agent-proxy per-tenant qps -> 10 for standard, 3 for free, 50 for enterprise. also add circuit-breaker for malformed structured outputs.
ryan: add a fallback route in router to send to text-generation-only model variant when structured_output=false. that will preserve responses but remove tool calls.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-73 "agent-proxy surge -> soft quarantine applied to free/dev". Severity: P2. Pager owners: eng-oncall.
alex: maria, tim — do the soft-quarantine now. jess publish status note: "We are experiencing degraded tool/function calling for some customers; we are rolling temporary mitigations and will update." Keep it terse.
maria: applying to plans free,dev -> now.
maria: applied. agent-proxy qdepth down from 1800 -> 220. error rate 502->2%.
tim: runtime policy pushed. per-tenant qps caps and circuit-breaker enabled. router routes legacy structured json to text-only fallback for scopes with flag.
jess: status page draft posted: "Investigating increased error rates for tool-based outputs. Temporary mitigations in place to limit tool calls for free and developer plans; paid accounts unaffected at this time. Monitoring."
alex: monitoring: token-level latency dropping ~35%, overall 5xxs reduced. hold for 10m then reassess.
ryan: once stable, we should prepare a targeted rollback plan: staged re-enable via canary tenants + telemetry gating (no spike in malformed jsons). also add a post-incident action: per-tenant scoring so we can preemptively throttle noisy clients.
alex: agreed. assign follow-ups after incident. thanks team. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime-policy-v1.4 -> canary -> 3 hosts.
maria: canary healthy. closing loop in 5m then update incident status.
alex: last check-in: system stable, tool call errors back to baseline for enterprise and standard, free/dev in soft-quarantine. closing incident bridge, will open follow-up ticket for telemetry and billing impact analysis.
jess: created support ticket bundle for affected tenants and queued template refund/credit where appropriate.
alex: closing thread. if anything regresses ping oncall."
